subsystems.name: Balloon envelope
subsystems.role: provides buoyancy to lift the launch platform to the stratosphere.

subsystems.name: Launch platform
subsystems.role: holds the rocket, points it, and releases it at altitude.

subsystems.name: Launch vehicle
subsystems.role: the rocket that ignites after release and carries payload to orbit.

subsystems.name: Tracking and telemetry
subsystems.role: monitors balloon and rocket, provides command and range safety.

subsystems.name: Ground support equipment
subsystems.role: inflates the balloon, integrates the rocket, and manages launch operations.

subsystems.name: Recovery system
subsystems.role: recovers the balloon platform after release, or disposes of it safely.

buildSteps.title: Design and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Engineers model balloon ascent, release dynamics, and rocket trajectory, including winds and thermal conditions.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the balloon
buildSteps.detail: Long sheets of thin polyethylene film are cut, heat-sealed into a large envelope, and fitted with a venting valve and load lines.

buildSteps.title: Build the launch platform
buildSteps.detail: A lightweight composite frame is assembled with a pointing mechanism, release clamps, and avionics, strong enough to hold the rocket but light enough to be lifted.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the rocket
buildSteps.detail: The rocket is mounted on the platform, checked out, and its guidance system is aligned for the expected release attitude.

buildSteps.title: Launch operations
buildSteps.detail: The balloon is inflated in a sheltered area, the platform attached, and the whole assembly released to ascend for one to two hours to 30–35 km.

buildSteps.title: Stratospheric release
buildSteps.detail: At altitude, the platform orients the rocket to the correct azimuth and elevation, then releases it.

buildSteps.title: Rocket ignition and ascent
buildSteps.detail: The rocket engine ignites, initially flying nearly horizontally to gain speed, then pitching up to reach orbit; the balloon is vented or cut loose.

buildSteps.title: Ground segment
buildSteps.detail: Radar and telemetry track the rocket, and range safety can destroy it if it veers off course.

buildSteps.title: Recovery
buildSteps.detail: The platform descends by parachute for reuse, or is disposed of over the ocean.

prerequisites.why: zero-pressure balloons routinely carry scientific payloads to 30–40 km.
many small rockets are commercially available, but they must be adapted for air launch.
demonstrated in suborbital rockoon tests since the 1950s, but not yet for orbital launch.
releasing a rocket from a balloon adds complexity compared to ground launch; software and sensors exist but need integration.
air launch from remote areas or international waters raises new regulatory questions; frameworks are being developed.

pathway.milestone: suborbital test flights and small orbital demonstration attempts
pathway.unlocks: proof of release and ignition at altitude.

pathway.milestone: first commercial small satellite launches from balloon platforms
pathway.unlocks: flexible launch services for cubesats and smallsats.

pathway.milestone: routine launches from multiple latitudes with days of notice
pathway.unlocks: rapid response and polar orbit access without fixed launch ranges.

pathway.milestone: scaling to larger payloads and reusable platforms
pathway.unlocks: lower cost per kilogram for smallsat operators.
